decided_findings.section: Task 1 Step 4 (web/next.config.ts, the production-only token gate — Choice 12, lap 1's PF-7); Task 2 Step 5 (web/package.json's build script); Task 16 Step 1 (the README's Deploy note); Choice 12
decided_findings.title: A VERCEL_ENV line in a web/.env file can still open the upload gate
decided_findings.terms_first: VERCEL_ENV: the variable Vercel sets at build time — production, preview or development. Lap 1's gate (Choice 12) uploads source maps only when it reads production. web/.env.local: a git-ignored file of local variables that `next build` and `next dev` load by themselves. `vercel env pull`: Vercel's command that copies a project's variables into such a file. SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN: the secret that lets a build upload source maps.
decided_findings.scenario: You want to check the production DSN on your machine, so you run `vercel env pull --environment=production` inside web/. Vercel writes web/.env.local with VERCEL_ENV="production", the real NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN, and SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN="[SENSITIVE]" (a placeholder for a Secret). Later you run `pnpm build`. Next.js loads web/.env.local before it reads next.config.ts, so the upload gate sees production and opens. With a real Sentry token in your shell, the build uploads source maps into the production project under the release name 'local'. Without one, it takes '[SENSITIVE]' as the token and every local build fails. And `pnpm dev` now reports your local errors into the production project.
decided_findings.whats_wrong: Next.js loads web/.env.production.local, .env.local, .env.production and .env before it evaluates next.config.ts, and fills in every variable the shell lacks. So the gate can read VERCEL_ENV from a file, not only from Vercel, and the README's 'never makes a local build upload' is then untrue.
evidence_quotes: Task 1 Step 4: const uploadToken = process.env.VERCEL_ENV === 'production' ? process.env.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN : undefined;
Task 16 Step 1, the README: so a `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` in your own shell — Sentry's command-line tools read that name — never makes a local build upload.
Next 16.3.6, dist/build/index.js:486-487: '// attempt to load global env values so they are available in next.config.js' then loadEnvConfig(dir, false, …); the config is loaded after, at :498.

ran: The real `next build` (Next 16.3.6) on scratch apps whose .env.local said VERCEL_ENV=production, with a next.config that printed the gate: no VERCEL_ENV in the shell -> 'VERCEL_ENV="production"; upload gate: true' (a .ts config too).
The same with the pin, sh -c 'VERCEL_ENV=$VERCEL_ENV next build' -> 'VERCEL_ENV=""; upload gate: false'. With VERCEL_ENV=production in the shell, as on Vercel -> 'upload gate: true'.
@next/env loadEnvConfig in fresh node processes: VERCEL_ENV unset -> becomes "production"; preset to '' -> stays ''. It never replaces a variable that is already present, even an empty one.
read_not_run: The Vercel CLI's source (packages/cli/src/commands/env/pull.ts): env pull writes every variable the API returns, dropping only three analytics ids; Secret variables are written as the placeholder '[SENSITIVE]'. Public CLI-written files show VERCEL_ENV="production" from production pulls. Vercel's docs do not say either way. The CLI was not run.

Task 6's init reads NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN, so a pulled real DSN makes `pnpm dev` report into the production project (against D5, production only); the e2e lane sets its own fake DSN, which a .env file cannot override.
verification.today: Not happening today: this worktree has no web/.env* file and no Vercel link; .gitignore covers .env files; a default `vercel env pull` writes VERCEL_ENV="development", which keeps the gate shut. It needs a deliberate production pull into web/.
verification.compatibility: The pin fits the build script as it is: app-version.mjs and assert-no-auth-token.mjs run as their own node processes and already read only the shell's VERCEL_ENV, so the release name and the gate can no longer disagree. web/vercel.json's buildCommand runs `pnpm run build`, and the e2e lane builds with `pnpm build`, so both get the pin. Next 16.3.6 reads VERCEL_ENV only as === 'preview', so '' and unset behave the same. The pin does not cover `pnpm dev`, which never uploads.

raw_reviewer_finding.title: A VERCEL_ENV line in web/.env files reopens local uploads
raw_reviewer_finding.section: Task 1 Step 4 — Wrap the Next config (Choice 12, the production-only token gate); Task 2 Step 5 — the build script; Task 16 Step 1 — the README's Deploy note
raw_reviewer_finding.why_it_matters: A local build can still upload with a developer's token. With a SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN in the shell (the premise of Choice 12, the production-only token gate) and VERCEL_ENV=production in any web/.env* file, the maps go up as release `local` into the production project, or the build fails on a read-only token. The cause: `next build` loads web/.env.production.local, .env.local, .env.production and .env before it evaluates next.config.ts, and fills in any variable the shell lacks (read in Next 16.3.6's loadConfigImpl and @next/env). The natural way to get the Production-only DSN for a local check, `vercel env pull --environment=production`, writes exactly that line (from Vercel's CLI documentation; not run here). Next never overwrites a variable that is already set, even to an empty value, so passing the shell's own VERCEL_ENV to next build makes the README's 'never makes a local build upload' true for every `pnpm run build`. Relied on: @sentry/nextjs 11.1.0, read from the local pnpm store, uploads only from the runAfterProductionCompile hook, which `Boolean(uploadToken)` switches on.
raw_reviewer_finding.suggested_fix: In Task 2 Step 5's build script, pass the shell's own value to next build — `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_VERSION=$(node scripts/app-version.mjs) VERCEL_ENV=$VERCEL_ENV next build` — and add one sentence under the snippet: 'VERCEL_ENV is passed through, and is empty when the shell has none: next build loads web/.env* files before next.config.ts and fills only variables that are missing, so a VERCEL_ENV line in one of those files cannot open the upload gate (Choice 12).'
evidence: Only a production build on Vercel reads the token: Sentry's own command-line tools read a variable of the same name from a developer's shell, and a local build must never upload with it.
so a `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` in your own shell — Sentry's command-line tools read that name — never makes a local build upload.
`VERCEL_ENV` needs Vercel's system environment variables exposed to the build
